title: U.S. House · Louisiana's 3rd District
area: Southwest Louisiana, including Acadiana and Lafayette.

context.text: Louisiana's 2026 U.S. House elections use a "majority vote" (all-party) system: every candidate, regardless of party, appears on one ballot on November 3, 2026. If no candidate wins a majority, the top two finishers advance to a December 12, 2026 general election. The partisan primary and runoff originally scheduled for May and June 2026 were canceled after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Louisiana v. Callais that the state's congressional map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, requiring a new map.

summary.text: Clay Higgins is the U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District, an Army veteran and former law enforcement officer who won the seat in a December 2016 runoff in his first race for public office. He is a core member of the House Freedom Caucus, a senior member of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, chairs its Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee, and also sits on the House Armed Services Committee.

background.text: Born August 24, 1961, in New Orleans; his family moved to Covington, Louisiana, when he was six. He graduated from Covington High School and attended Louisiana State University.
Army veteran; his campaign website says he received his initial police training as a military police officer in the U.S. Army.

Spent much of his career in law enforcement, and maintains an active commission and Louisiana State POST certification. The Advocate described him in 2016 as a reserve deputy for the Lafayette City Marshal's Office and a former captain with the St. Landry Parish Sheriff's Office.
The Advocate described him as a viral Crime Stoppers video star and reported that he ran as a tough-talking outsider in his first bid for public office.

Finished second in the November 8, 2016 open-seat primary (26 percent, behind Scott Angelle's 29 percent) and defeated Angelle, a fellow Republican, in the December 10, 2016 runoff by about 12 percentage points; took office January 3, 2017.

Serves as a senior member of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee and as Chairman of its Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee; also serves on the House Armed Services Committee's Subcommittees on Seapower and Projection Forces and on Readiness.
His official biography describes him as a core member of the House Freedom Caucus and says the Center for Effective Lawmaking ranked him among the most effective Republican legislators in the House.
Resides in Lafayette with his wife, Becca.

priorities.text: Site describes him as advancing "Constitutionalist principles" and as a champion for smaller government, lower taxes, secure borders and individual freedoms.

positions.summary: States that life begins at conception and that he has cosponsored and voted for legislation to prohibit federal funding for abortions, defund Planned Parenthood and restrict late-term abortions.
positions.quote: I believe strongly that we should do all we can as a society to protect the sanctity of life, which unquestionably begins at conception.

positions.summary: Issued a statement urging the Senate to pass the SAVE America Act, which would require documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote.
positions.quote: We demand a fight for the SAVE America Act in the Senate.

record.text: Serves as Chairman of the Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, where his office says he investigates government corruption; also serves on the House Armed Services Committee's Subcommittees on Seapower and Projection Forces and on Readiness.
Is a core member of the House Freedom Caucus.

summary.text: Tia LeBrun is a teacher and curriculum leader from Terrebonne Parish and a member of the United Houma Nation, running as a candidate with no party affiliation for Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District. She ran for the same seat as a Democrat in 2022 and is campaigning on education access, healthcare affordability and insurance reform.

background.text: Born and raised in Terrebonne Parish as a member of the United Houma Nation; according to her campaign website, she is the daughter of three generations of working-class service-industry workers.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Louisiana State University (2004) and a graduate degree from the University of New Orleans (2012); her campaign website says she had her first child before studying at LSU and later worked two jobs while teaching.

Works as an educator and administrator. According to her campaign website, she was named Teacher of the Year at Lake Charles Boston High School in 2007, was honored as Louisiana Public Broadcasting's American Graduate in 2015, and was Teacher of the Year of the Louisiana Foreign Language Teachers' Association in 2016.

Her campaign website says she was a member of the Louisiana Foreign Language Teachers' Association from 2005 to 2017, has served on the Louisiana Consortium of Immersion Schools board since 2016, and has served on the Council for the Development of French in Louisiana board since 2019.
Ran for this seat as a Democrat in the November 8, 2022 all-party primary, receiving 21,172 votes (9.4 percent); Clay Higgins won outright.
Her campaign website says she and her husband share six children and she has four grandchildren.

priorities.text: Says Louisiana families are "being crushed by the highest insurance rates in the nation" and calls for a national plan for insurance affordability and disaster mitigation.
priorities.quote: Louisiana families are also being crushed by the highest insurance rates in the nation. We need a national plan for insurance affordability and disaster mitigation that protects homeowners, drivers, and small businesses—before the next storm hits.

priorities.text: Wants affordable healthcare and childcare for every parent, and is "fighting for paid family leave, healthcare not tied to employment, universal preschool, and two years of free community college."
priorities.quote: Every parent should have access to affordable healthcare, childcare, and education. Families should be able to grow, learn, and live well without going broke. That's why I'm fighting for paid family leave, healthcare not tied to employment, universal preschool, and two years of free community college.

priorities.text: Says she believes in "personal freedom—the right to make decisions about your own body, your family, and your future without government or corporate interference."
priorities.quote: Above all, I believe in personal freedom—the right to make decisions about your own body, your family, and your future without government or corporate interference.

positions.summary: Says she believes in personal freedom, "the right to make decisions about your own body," without government interference.
positions.quote: Above all, I believe in personal freedom—the right to make decisions about your own body, your family, and your future without government or corporate interference.

positions.summary: Calls for healthcare not tied to employment and affordable healthcare for every parent.
Campaigns for paid family leave and universal preschool.

candidates.name: John Day

summary.text: John Day is a Democratic candidate on the ballot for Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District.

background.text: Born in Shreveport, raised in Lake Charles, and graduated from Sam Houston High School, according to his Ballotpedia survey.
Served in the U.S. Navy beginning in 1994.
Works as a professional writer and, in his words, is working toward producing film projects.
Says he is married to Amanda Hardy Day and that they have four grown children.

priorities.text: Lists lower costs, better pay, safer communities and storm protection as what he would deliver.
priorities.quote: I’m running to deliver results you can feel at home: lower costs, better pay, safer communities, and real storm protection — with honesty, accountability, and respect for taxpayers.

priorities.text: Lists expanding rural care and keeping patients in charge of healthcare decisions as a campaign theme.
priorities.quote: Protect your right to make your own medical decisions, expand rural care, and put patients — not politicians — in charge of healthcare.

priorities.text: Lists keeping families in their homes and supporting first-time buyers as a campaign theme.
priorities.quote: Keep families in their homes. Support first-time buyers.

candidates.researchNotes: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2026) reviewed; the only statement matching the guide's issues is the energy position already listed. No campaign website found.

statements.quote: an all-of-the-above energy strategy — supporting the oil and gas jobs that power our economy and investing in renewable energy to lower costs, strengthen our grid, and secure our future.
statements.context: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

candidates.name: Priscilla Gonzalez

summary.text: Priscilla Gonzalez is a Democratic candidate on the ballot for Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District. A marketing director born in McAllen, Texas, she ran for the same seat in 2024.

background.text: Born in McAllen, Texas, and earned a bachelor's degree from Fort Hays State University.
Her career experience includes working as a marketing director.
Ran for this seat as a Democrat in the November 5, 2024 primary, receiving 59,834 votes (18.7 percent); Clay Higgins won outright with 70.6 percent.

priorities.text: Says she is committed to a justice system that emphasizes rehabilitation.
priorities.quote: I am dedicated to creating a fair and equitable justice system that prioritizes rehabilitation over punishment.

priorities.text: Describes access to healthcare as a fundamental right and lists plans to improve services and reduce costs.
priorities.quote: Access to quality healthcare is a fundamental right.

priorities.text: Says she will pursue initiatives to increase teacher salaries.
priorities.quote: Teachers are the backbone of our education system. Learn about my commitment to increasing teacher salaries and ensuring they receive the respect and compensation they deserve.

positions.summary: Says Louisiana should continue to expand Medicaid eligibility.
positions.quote: Louisiana should continue to expand Medicaid eligibility to help more low-income people and families.

statements.quote: Long-term hurricane vulnerability reduction in Louisiana depends on addressing climate change and its effects.
statements.context: On her campaign website's hurricanes page

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign site prisforcongress.com reviewed (issues pages). Several pages are written about Louisiana state policy and are headed 'State Representative'; positions are taken only where the text directly addresses a guide issue. Did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 survey.

candidates.name: Caleb Walker

summary.text: Caleb Walker is a Democratic candidate on the ballot for Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District.

priorities.text: Lists lowering the cost of living as a priority issue.
priorities.quote: Groceries, insurance, housing, and everyday costs are squeezing Louisiana families.

priorities.text: Lists investing in people, including teacher pay, as a priority issue.
priorities.quote: Caleb will fight to increase teacher pay and make the first $50,000 of every educator’s salary exempt from federal income tax.

priorities.text: Lists defending the coastline and growing jobs as a priority issue.
priorities.quote: Caleb will fight for coastal restoration, stronger flood protection, and storm-resilient infrastructure that safeguards our homes, businesses, seafood industry, and coastal communities.

statements.quote: Caleb will confront global warming with practical, science-based solutions while supporting responsible carbon-capture projects that reduce emissions, protect communities, create jobs, and preserve Louisiana’s energy leadership.
statements.context: On his campaign website's issues page (third person)

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign site calebforcongress.com reviewed; it states priorities but takes a side on few guide issues. Only one statement (climate) found. Did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 survey.

candidates.name: Kate Cotten

summary.text: Kate Cotten is a Republican candidate on the ballot for Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District. BallotReady lists her work history as owner of a business called Cotton's Downtown and former executive director of ResCare.

background.text: According to BallotReady, she has owned Cotton's Downtown since 2014 and was executive director of ResCare from 2007 to 2014.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or public statements found; Ballotpedia lists no website and no survey response.

researchNotes: Priscilla Gonzalez's and Caleb Walker's campaign websites and John Day's 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey were used for the items shown. Kate Cotten did not complete the survey and no campaign website or public statements were found for her beyond her name and party on the ballot. Biographies for Tia LeBrun and John Day draw on their Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers (Priscilla Gonzalez completed one in 2024 only). No campaign website or public statements were found for Caleb Walker or Kate Cotten beyond their names and party affiliation on the ballot; Kate Cotten's work history comes from BallotReady, and no biographical details were found for Caleb Walker.
